channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: AI Provides ‘Zero Payoff’ to S&P 493 Outside Tech, Apollo Economist Says
item.description: Despite the significant investments ploughed into artificial intelligence it has provided “zero payoff” to corporate America outside of technology, according to Apollo Global Management Inc. Chief Economist Torsten Slok.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Smith

item.title: SoftBank’s Son Plans $50 Billion Malaysia Tech Outlay, PM Says
item.description: Masayoshi Son of SoftBank Group Corp. chose locations in Malaysia for $50 billion in technology investments, the country’s prime minister said, an outlay that would accelerate the billionaire’s global bet on AI infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Anuradha Raghu

item.title: UAE Shuts More Beaches as It Deals with Oil Spill in Gulf
item.description: The United Arab Emirates shut more beaches after an oil spill in the Persian Gulf raised concerns over environmental and health impacts.
item.dc:creator: Sara Gharaibeh

item.title: Australia Police Chief Says Angry Debate Adds Risks to Lawmakers
item.description: Acrimonious political debate in Australia is escalating risks to legislators, one of the country’s most senior police officers said after a lawmaker suffered serious injuries following an alleged attack.
item.dc:creator: David Stringer

item.title: Sinking Profits Turn China’s $3.5 Trillion Stock Rout Into Trap
item.description: Pessimism has gripped Chinese stocks, with no end in sight for a deepening selloff as investors confront the realities of an economy that’s weak enough to erode corporate profits but not to trigger forceful new stimulus.
item.dc:creator: Jeanny Yu

item.title: AI Boom Faces a Growing Public Backlash
item.description: The Atlantic CEO Nicholas Thompson tells Bloomberg This Weekend that AI offers powerful tools for businesses but poses significant risks to media, while its broader economic impact continues to lag behind rapidly advancing capabilities. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Thompson also discusses the discipline of distance running and how the sport shaped his relationship with his father and became an organizing force in his life. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Boom Brings New Business to Matchmakers
item.description: Linx Dating founder and CEO Amy Andersen tells Bloomberg This Weekend that newly wealthy AI creators are fueling demand for high-end matchmaking as busy professionals seek an alternative to dating apps. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Andersen explains how her firm vets and recruits potential partners for selective clients, with matchmaking packages that can exceed $500,000. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Making Advanced MicroChips Takes a Global Ecosystem
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Gideon Lewis-Kraus explains how advanced chipmaking depends on a deeply interconnected global network of specialized companies, including ASML and TSMC, making semiconductor supply chains extraordinarily difficult to replicate or relocate. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Lewis-Kraus describes the remarkable engineering behind ASML’s EUV machines and why rebuilding a semiconductor ecosystem in the US is a generational project rather than a simple exercise in reshoring. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Technical Colleges Bet on AI-Driven Demand for Skilled Workers
item.description: Technical colleges are betting a surge in demand for skilled workers will lift profits, though the payoff may take time as they expand campuses and programs to accommodate more students.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Phua

item.title: Bank of Israel Slams Netanyahu’s Anti-Sanctions Crypto Proposal
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu floated using cryptocurrency to get around potential financial sanctions on Israel, prompting a strongly-worded rebuke from the central bank.
item.dc:creator: Galit Altstein
